''' Laurence Eaves''' [[CBE]], [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]], [[Learned Society of Wales|FLSW]] (born 13 May 1948) is a Welsh [[physicist]]<ref name="debretts">{{cite web |url=http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/e/19580/Laurence+EAVES.aspx |title=Prof Laurence Eaves, CBE, FRS Authorised Biography – Debrett's People of Today, Prof Laurence Eaves, CBE, FRS Profile |website=www.debretts.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130619125907/http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/e/19580/Laurence+EAVES.aspx |archive-date=2013-06-19}}</ref> and professor at [[University of Nottingham]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nottingham.ac.uk/physics/people/laurence.eaves|title=Staff Listing - the University of Nottingham}}</ref>

==Life==
Laurence Eaves was born in [[Pentre]], in the [[Rhondda valley]], [[Wales]] in 1948 and was educated at Rhondda County Grammar School, Porth, and at [[Corpus Christi College, Oxford]], where he took [[First class honours|Firsts]] in Physics and Mathematics Moderations and in Physics Final Honours.  He gained his DPhil at the [[Clarendon Laboratory]], Oxford, working under the supervision of [[R. A. Stradling]] on the interaction between conduction electrons and phonons in [[semiconductor]]s at high magnetic fields.

Following a Research Lectureship at [[Christ Church, Oxford]] from 1972 to 1974, and a [[Miller Research Fellows|Miller Fellowship]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], he was appointed to a Lectureship in Physics at the [[University of Nottingham]], UK in 1976, where he has been a Professor of Physics since 1984.<ref name="debretts"/>

In 2011, he was elected a [[Learned Society of Wales|Fellow of the Learned Society of Wales]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wales |first=The Learned Society of |title=Laurence Eaves |url=https://www.learnedsociety.wales/fellow/laurence-eaves-3/ |access-date=2023-08-30 |website=The Learned Society of Wales |language=en-US}}</ref>

His research interests have focussed on the motion of [[electron]]s in [[nanostructure]]s in the presence of strong electric fields.  Publications include spatial mapping of the electronic wavefunction in semiconducting [[quantum dot]]s, the quantum [[Chaotic dynamical system|chaotic dynamics]] of electrons, and the properties of electronic devices in which electrons tunnel through a potential barrier.  He is also interested in using high magnetic fields to study a range of physical phenomena including droplet [[hydrodynamics]].  His present research is focused on the electronic properties of [[heterostructure]]s and devices made from [[graphene]] and other two-dimensional crystals.
